sections.h2: Where is Middletown, CT, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Middletown is a city on the west bank of the Connecticut River in Middlesex County, about 16 miles south of Hartford. The 2020 census counted 47,717 residents, and the city covers 42.36 square miles, so it is geographically large.

The size comes from a 1923 consolidation of the city and the surrounding town. Middletown shares borders with Cromwell, Portland, East Hampton, Haddam, Durham, Middlefield, Berlin and Meriden. Portland and East Hampton lie across the river, so no land boundary connects them to Middletown.

Route 9 runs alongside the river and bisects the city. Wikipedia notes that highway construction in the 1950s demolished historic neighborhoods and separated downtown from the waterfront.

sections.h2: What is the history of Middletown?
sections.html:
English settlers established the town in 1651 under the name Mattabesett, the name of a Wangunk village, and renamed it Middletown in 1653. The name reflects its position about halfway between Windsor and Saybrook on the river.

The city grew as a river port, then as a manufacturing center. Products included marine hardware, typewriters, and silver plate. Wesleyan University was founded in 1831, and in 1841 Middletown established the state's first public high school.

Connecticut General Hospital for the Insane opened here in 1868, and it now operates as Connecticut Valley Hospital. Middletown was the Middlesex County seat until county government was eliminated in the 1960s. It still hosts the Middlesex Superior Court.

Floods in 1927 and 1936 and the Great New England Hurricane of 1938 all hit the city.

Wikipedia lists several named areas in Middletown, each with a different character. Downtown runs along Main Street near Wesleyan, with shops and restaurants, and a revitalization effort has focused on the North End.

  • Highland: the westernmost neighborhood, and the only part of the city Interstate 91 passes through.
  • Westfield: a mostly residential area in the northwest, just south of Cromwell.
  • Miramichi: a residential area in the southwest, near Middlefield.
  • Newfield Heights: a commercial area north of the city center.
  • Bretton Heights and South Farms: mostly residential areas.
  • Maromas: largely industrial and mostly uninhabited, home to a Pratt and Whitney facility.

The west side of the city runs along the Metacomet Ridge, including Higby Mountain, and the 50-mile Mattabesett Trail crosses it. A house on a ridge slope and a house near Pameacha Pond or Crystal Lake will present different inspection issues to a buyer.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in Middletown?
sections.html:
Healthcare, aerospace, logistics and education lead the local employment list. The city's 2023 annual financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, ranks Middlesex Health Systems first.

That mix supports a steady base of owners and renters. It also means a lot of Middletown sellers are relocating for a job, retiring from one, or inheriting a house from someone who worked locally for decades.

sections.h2: What are Middletown households and housing like?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 20,081 households and 21,671 housing units in Middletown, with 7.3 percent of units vacant. About 54 percent of units were owner-occupied.

Households are small. The average household size was 2.14, and 37.1 percent of households were one person living alone. Median age was 38.2.

The city's housing stock includes the older neighborhoods around downtown, 1960s suburban developments, and cluster communities such as The Farms in Westlake, an 84-house development from 1969 with common land.

sections.h2: How do you get around Middletown?
sections.html:
Middletown is served by Route 9, Interstate 91 on its western edge, and the Arrigoni Bridge across the river to Portland, which opened in 1938. Route 154, the old Middlesex Turnpike, runs along the west side of the river valley.

  • River Valley Transit serves Middletown and runs to Old Saybrook, where riders connect to Amtrak and Shore Line East.
  • CT Transit provides local and express service to Hartford, plus express service to New Haven.
  • New Britain Transportation Company runs a connecting service to New Britain.
  • Bradley International Airport and Tweed New Haven Airport are the nearest commercial airports.

Meriden Markham Municipal Airport and Goodspeed Airport in East Haddam offer general aviation.

Middletown Public Schools operates the public schools, including Middletown High School. Vinal Technical High School is the technical high school in the city.

Private options include Saint John Paul II Regional Catholic School for elementary grades, and Xavier High School (boys) and Mercy High School (girls). Post-secondary choices are Wesleyan University and Middlesex Community College.

sections.h2: How is Middletown's sewer service handled?
sections.html:
Middletown's wastewater now goes to the Mattabassett Sewer District treatment plant in nearby Cromwell. In November 2012, voters approved a $37 million initiative to make that move, replacing the plant the city had operated on the Connecticut River bank.

The city has talked about redeveloping the old riverfront plant site. Whether a particular street is on public sewer or on a septic system is something to confirm with the city before you list, because buyers and lenders often ask.

sections.h2: How do Middletown property taxes work, including the fire districts?
sections.html:
Middletown computes taxes for a fiscal year that runs July 1 through June 30, and bills them in two installments, due July 1 and January 1. Interest is 1.5 percent per month, or 18 percent a year, on unpaid balances after the first business day of the month following the due date.

The city's tax page adds a point sellers often miss: each fire district sets its own mill rate. The City Fire District tax is included in the real estate bill, but the South Fire District and the Westfield Fire District bill and collect separately. If your house is in one of those districts, ask the title company to check both bills.

  • Bills go to the owner of record on the October 1 Grand List date, and that name stays until the next assessment date.
  • Banks that escrow taxes must request bills from the collector, so tell your lender about a sale.
  • There is no charge for copies of tax bills.

Check the city's mill rate page for the current rate, since it changes by year.

sections.h2: What does a Middletown seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
Connecticut's conveyance tax is paid by the seller at recording. The statute sets 0.75 percent for the state and 0.25 percent for the municipality on a standard home sale, with a higher state rate on the portion of a residential price over $800,000.

The seller, attorney or agent files Form OP-236 with the town clerk, and the deed cannot be recorded until the tax is paid. The city's probate court district also covers Cromwell, Portland, Middlefield and Haddam, which can matter if you are selling an estate property and need the court's involvement.

faqs.q: Is Middletown, CT the county seat of Middlesex County?
faqs.a: Middletown was the county seat from 1785 until Connecticut eliminated county government. It still hosts the Middlesex Superior Court and its judicial district.

faqs.q: When are Middletown real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate taxes are due in two installments, July 1 and January 1. Late payments accrue interest at 1.5 percent per month.

faqs.q: Do Middletown fire districts affect my tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The City Fire District tax is part of the real estate bill. The South Fire District and Westfield Fire District bill and collect separately, so a house there can have two bills.

faqs.q: What are the biggest employers in Middletown?
faqs.a: Middlesex Health Systems, Pratt and Whitney (RTX), Connecticut Valley Hospital, FedEx, the school system and Wesleyan University lead the city's 2023 list.

faqs.q: Who files the Connecticut conveyance tax return when I sell?
faqs.a: The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded. The town clerk cannot record the deed until the tax is paid.
